properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. @ajs, 2026-09-30: "If the design is held in flo2.io for reflow2, could just before a PR, could we export the design, download it locally and then update the change log accordingly and then merge? … We could also remove the design completely from the reflow2 [repo] and then only have to worry about how to figure out how to update the change log?"

THE PAIN, measured: every PR hand-edits CHANGELOG.md's Unreleased section, so parallel PRs conflict there. On 2026-09-30, fix 2 (#641) edited it while three other branches waited to merge main. req:the-changelog-is-the-one-record-of-what-changed-and-no-required-upgrade-step-is-lost (accepted) makes CHANGELOG.md the record, and no upgrade step may be lost.

OPTIONS, none chosen:
(a) As today: each PR hand-edits Unreleased. It costs a conflict per parallel PR.
(b) ONE FRAGMENT FILE PER PR (changelog.d/<pr>.md, the towncrier pattern). The release cut assembles the fragments. No conflicts, independent of where the design lives, and the author writes the upgrade step while they still know it.
(c) DRAFTED FROM THE DESIGN AT THE RELEASE CUT. changelog_view renders the ChangeEvents since the last deployed release (cap:changelog-view). Each PR records its consumer-facing note, including any upgrade step, on its own ChangeEvent, so the design is the single source.
(d) @AJS'S: drafted from the design at EACH PR, from a fresh export, just before merge.

SIZE AND COUNTERS:
- (b) is small and standard. Its counter: a second record beside the design, which can disagree with it.
- (c) is medium, and two measured obstacles stand in the way:
  - fact:changelog-view-is-step-two-of-the-cut-and-returns-nothing-for-a-real-cut (2026-09-03, not re-measured);
  - fact:root-cause-no-served-read-answers-since-last-time-2026-09-28: the core stores no write time, so "since the last release" is reckoned by epoch order over pinned ChangeEvents only.
  changelog_view also says itself that it holds what moved, never what it costs a consumer (needs_a_human). So the upgrade-step text must be captured somewhere at PR time either way.
- (d) inherits (c)'s obstacles, and a per-PR draft still conflicts in Unreleased unless each draft lands in its own file. So (d) collapses into (b) or (c).

2026-10-03 — SETTLED ON (b), ONE FRAGMENT FILE PER PR, on @ajs's word.
- Asked whether to fix the queue of approved PRs that kept conflicting, he answered: "yes, need to implement small per-PR pieces".
- The proposal he accepted: "CHANGELOG fragments assembled at release, and design records committed as per-PR fragments … rather than a full export per PR".
- WHY (c) and (d) lost: they need the upgrade-step text captured at PR time anyway, and changelog_view's two obstacles above are still unmeasured. (b) is small and standard, and removes the conflict now.
- The DESIGN-RECORD half is not settled here. It belongs to the accepted req:the-saved-design-merges-correctly-under-gits-ordinary-merge, and the measured cost that brought both to a head is in this decision's companion finding of 2026-10-03.
- This is the fix program's item 13, the first item after the second three-agent trial.
properties.name: SETTLED 2026-10-03 — CHANGELOG.md is written as one fragment file per PR, assembled at the release cut (option b)
properties.rationale: The changelog conflict is the half of @ajs's move question that does not depend on where the design lives. Options (b) and (c) remove it whether reflow2's design stays local or moves to flo2.io.
